rationale: Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is essentially an equal-weight blend of two well-documented anomalies (capex/asset growth and R&D intensity) rather than a genuine interaction, since SUMRANK cannot distinguish "hard-asset growth without intangible backing" from a firm that is merely high on one leg.

This is close to a direct rediscovery of the acquisition/external-growth component of the asset-growth anomaly (aqc/lagged assets), and adding DELTA(gdwl) double-counts the same transactions rather than adding an intangible-specific dimension.

Well-constructed and coherent, but intangible-adjusted (Peters–Taylor style) capital growth is already published and will be very highly correlated with plain asset growth, making this a refinement of a known anomaly rather than a cross-theme discovery.

The indicator logic correctly switches on for sub-2% R&D-to-sales firms and the negative sign matches the expression, but zeroing out R&D-intensive firms plants them in the middle of the cross-section as a large mass point, which will dilute and destabilize the sorted spread relative to a proper subsample test.

A genuinely novel, economically coherent composition-of-investment state variable whose positive sign matches the expression; the main risk is the large mass point at exactly zero from non-R&D firms and an unstable denominator when capx+xrd is near zero.

Beyond being a blend of the known net-external-financing and R&D-intensity anomalies, it is internally inconsistent: xrd is not coalesced, so firms with no reported R&D program—the exact "cheap capital, no innovation" cohort the hypothesis targets—are dropped from coverage.
